summary: A Persian imperial monarchy joining territories from the eastern Mediterranean to Central and South Asia through satrapal government.
currency: Gold daric and silver siglos; regional currencies also circulated.
rulers: Selected rulers: Cyrus II, 559–530 BCE; Darius I, 522–486 BCE; Xerxes I, 486–465 BCE.
economy: Provincial tribute and long-distance communications supported a monarchy governing diverse regional economies.
military: Conquest incorporated Lydia, Babylonia and Egypt; campaigns against mainland Greek states encountered major defeats.
contributions: Satrapal administration, imperial roads and monumental architecture connected diverse peoples across a large state.
origin: Cyrus defeated the Median king Astyages in 550 BCE, then conquered neighboring kingdoms.
decline: Alexander defeated Persian armies and seized provinces; Darius III was killed in 330 BCE.
periodNote: 550 BCE marks Cyrus’s conquest of Media. Sources sometimes use 331 BCE, the battle of Gaugamela, rather than Darius III’s death in 330.
